newsitem.title: INDIA: Astrologers join India politicians in quest for PM.
newsitem.headline: Astrologers join India politicians in quest for PM.

text.p: Astrologers, politicians and rebellious deputies joined in a desperate hunt for the elusive successor to ousted Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda on Sunday as prospects of early polls loomed.

Politicians said Deve Gowda's 15-party coalition and his ally-turned-foe, the Congress party, were each battling to keep their deputies together amid reports of a threatened rebellion, prompted by poll fears and lurking political uncertainty.
The United Front officially denied reports of dissent among its coalition partners over Deve Gowda's leadership of the group despite his government's defeat in a trust vote on Friday.
But party members said pressure was mounting on Deve Gowda to help avert elections even if it meant stepping down as the United Front's leader.
State radio, however, quoted Deve Gowda as saying the alliance would face elections.
The Congress, which precipitated the crisis by pulling the props out from under Deve Gowda, was equally worried.

"No member of parliament wants an election," said Congress deputy A.R. Antulay, angry over party president Sitaram Kesri's decision on March 30 to withdraw make-or-break support for Deve Gowda's 10-month-old government.

"Everybody is scrambling to survive the disaster which nobody wanted. Only a very few people worked for this crisis to happen," Antulay, a former chief minister of India's wealthiest state of Maharashtra, told reporters.
Other disgruntled party leaders said privately they would press for Kesri's sacking at a meeting of the party's Congress Working Committee scheduled on Monday.
"We are hopeful of forming a government with the United Front," a former Congress minister told Reuters.
He said the alliance's official position that it would not support either Congress or the rightwing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in a bid to form a government could be changed.
With politicians apparently unable to make a breakthrough, they turned to astrologers for psychic help. Newspapers said some businessmen and even journalists had joined them, too.
"A three of pentacles has been dominating the picture," a Delhi-based astrologer told some politicians visiting her soon after Deve Gowda's defeat in parliament on Friday.

"That indicates that some wise men will join hands to work within a fraternity. It doesn't look like mid-term polls are likely," she told Reuters later, scrutinising a series of mysterious figures on the tarot cards.
"According to my calculations Mr Gowda will complete his term," the Asian Age daily quoted the prime minister's astrologer Vishwapathi Sastri as saying.
The defeated government was formed last June by the alliance, which has 178 lawmakers, with support from the Congress, which has 140 deputies in the 545-member lower house.
The United Front and Congress closed ranks last year to oust a 12-day-old government formed by the BJP, which controls 193 deputies.
President Shankar Dayal Sharma has asked Deve Gowda to stay on as caretaker prime minister while efforts are made to forge a new governing majority in the hung parliament.
The front was still weighing its options, and there were differences within the coalition, a Deve Gowda aide said on Saturday.
"Deve Gowda says they (the alliance) can do well in an election. But there are others in the United Front who do not want a mid-term poll," he said.
